name: veslint
description: typescript-eslint rules from veslint, a TypeScript linter that talks to the TypeScript 7 compiler: problems, fixes and suggestions in the editor.

commands.title: Fix All Problems That Have a Fix

veslint.path.markdownDescription: The veslint binary: a name to look up in `PATH`, an absolute path, or a path relative to the workspace folder. The binary looks for the TypeScript 7 compiler in the `node_modules` next to it.

veslint.config.markdownDescription: The configuration to lint with: an ESLint configuration file (`eslint.config.mjs` and the like, which needs `bun`), the JSON that `veslint --print-config` prints, or a JSON with a `rules` section. Relative to the workspace folder. When empty, the `eslint.config.*` file at the root of the folder is used.

veslint.project.markdownDescription: The `tsconfig.json` to use (`--project`). When empty, veslint takes the closest one to each file.

enumDescriptions: Lint a file when it is opened, saved, and as you type (its unsaved text, through the veslint server), after `veslint.typingDelay`.
Lint a file when it is opened and when it is saved.
Lint only with the veslint commands.
veslint.run.markdownDescription: When files are linted. Unsaved text is linted through `veslint --server`; with a veslint without it, only saved text is.

veslint.typingDelay.markdownDescription: Milliseconds that typing must pause before a file is linted, when `veslint.run` is `onType`. `0` lints after every change: a lint that the next change makes useless is skipped if it has not started, and given up by the server if it has; the problems of a text that changed while it was linted are not shown. A larger value lints less often while you type, which saves CPU on large files.

veslint.severity.markdownDescription: How the problems of the rules are shown. veslint's output does not tell whether a rule is set to `error` or to `warn`, so all of them get this severity; unused directive comments and configuration errors keep their own.

veslint.timeout.description: Milliseconds after which a run that has not finished is stopped.
